Date: 2026-03-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sofia Kale (CSM), Priya Shah (Elysian Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (Elysian Security Eng), Amir Patel (Elysian IT Ops), Nina Rao (Elysian Compliance)
summary: High-level security and provisioning planning for SAML + SCIM integration and least-privilege RBAC model. Discussed Okta as IdP, SCIM group mapping, SAML attribute assertions, RBAC role design, break-glass and audit logging requirements. Agreed pilot runway and deliverables: Okta metadata, mapping templates, sample role YAML, and a SCIM pilot kickoff week of 2026-03-16.

KMS/encryption key flow and HSM options
Audit logs, SIEM ingestion, retention & residency
Private vs hosted deployment considerations (Redwood Private)
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll call?
[00:00:06] Priya: Priya here.
[00:00:07] Liam: Liam on security.
[00:00:08] Amir: Amir from ops.
[00:00:09] Nina: Nina from compliance.
[00:00:12] Omar: Omar, Redwood SE.
[00:00:14] Maya: Great. We're here to walk through the identity flightpath — SAML and SCIM setup and how you want to map groups to roles, plus a look at audit and key management. We'll try to keep it practical.
[00:00:28] Priya: High level: we use Okta as our IdP, provisioning via SCIM for most apps, and we have a few service accounts that are manual. Our compliance team wants least-privilege RBAC and good audit trails.
[00:00:42] Maya: Perfect, that's aligned with most of our enterprise customers. Omar, want to start on SAML attributes?
[00:00:47] Omar: Sure. For Redwood, the minimal SAML assertion we recommend is: NameID (email), email, givenName, familyName, and groups. Groups are optional but helpful if you want SCIM off first, you can still do role mapping by group claim. We also often ask for an employee_id or subject to tie to existing identity sources.
[00:01:05] Liam: Quick question — how do you handle multiple group claims and nested groups? Our Okta setup has nested groups for team->role.
[00:01:14] Omar: Good point. We support comma-separated group strings and also multiple assertion attributes. For nested groups it's best to flatten at Okta via an expression or to provision only the role-level groups. If you send us the Okta expression you use we can recommend the mapping.
[00:01:29] Amir: We also want SCIM to provision machine/service accounts for pipelines. Are there limits on service-account provisioning?
[00:01:37] Omar: Not hard limits for the pilot; we do rate-limit at scale but for POC volumes it's fine. For long-lived service keys we typically recommend those be created via Private deployment or with customer-managed KMS so you control rotation.
[00:01:49] Nina: On compliance, retention for audit logs is important — we need 7 years for some artifacts, but logs we usually keep 1-3 years. How does Redwood handle audit export and SIEM integrations?
[00:02:00] Maya: We export structured audit logs (JSON) via S3 or syslog and support Splunk/Elastic ingestion patterns. Retention is configurable on your side if you use S3, and we can provide export hooks — Omar, do you want to add details?
[00:02:12] Omar: Yeah. Our Console can stream logs to a customer bucket in the region you pick, or push to a syslog endpoint. For Splunk we do HTTP Event Collector / HEC config. For retention, if you pick Redwood Private you can enforce local retention policies; hosted customers usually export to their own archive.
[00:02:29] Priya: Data residency is critical. Elysian requires EU residency for EU customer data. We might be split across US and EU. How granular is region policy?
[00:02:38] Maya: We support region-level routing. You can pin certain customers to EU regions and others to US. For Private, everything stays in your VPC. For Hosted we provide region selection and we log the region per request.
[00:02:50] Liam: KMS — can we bring our own key (BYOK) and HSM? We have a hardware security module for high-sensitivity keys.
[00:02:58] Omar: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS integrations and offer an HSM-backed option for Private deployments. For hosted, BYOK via AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault is typical; for air-gapped/on-prem we can integrate with on-prem HSMs. We will diagram the key flow for you.
[00:03:15] Amir: About RBAC design: we want least-privilege. Typical roles we use are viewer, deployer, admin, and auditor. How do you recommend mapping Okta groups to Redwood roles?
[00:03:27] Omar: A common pattern is SCIM groups named with a prefix, e.g., redwood_role_admin, redwood_role_deployer. SCIM pushes groups to Redwood and our SCIM->RBAC connector creates roles or assigns existing roles. For finer grain, you can use attribute-based roles where SAML attributes include allowed_actions.
[00:03:43] Priya: Do you have policy templates? We want examples that match financial services SOPs.
[00:03:47] Omar: Yes, we'll share YAML templates: least-privilege admin, read-only auditor (audit with no config change), deployer with model deployment rights but not admin controls. We'll include canary deploy exemptions and how to limit model rollouts to specific teams.
[00:04:02] Maya: Also we recommend break-glass processes: emergency SSO bypass for on-call for a short window with full logging. Liam, do you have constraints around break-glass approvals?
[00:04:12] Liam: We require two-person approval for break-glass and all actions must be logged and emailed to the security mailbox.
[00:04:18] Omar: Our break-glass flow supports time-limited elevated tokens and we log the requestor and approver in the audit trail. We can hook approvals to Jira/ServiceNow as well.
[00:04:28] Priya: About provisioning cadence — we want SCIM to run near-real-time, but are ok with a minute or two delay. Any gotchas?
[00:04:35] Omar: SCIM is near real-time. For group membership churn we recommend using SCIM patch operations to avoid full re-provision cycles. Also watch for large bulk updates: throttle settings kick in. We'll show a best-practice configuration.
[00:04:48] Amir: Network egress for hosted — do you publish egress IPs or ranges? We need to allowlist.
[00:04:53] Maya: We publish a stable set of egress CIDRs per region for Dedicated and a rolling list for hosted, but for pilot we can provide specific IPs. For Private, obviously no egress.
[00:05:03] Nina: Audit: what fields are mandatory in logs? We need actor, action, resource, timestamp, request_id, and the assertion used for auth.
[00:05:11] Omar: We include request_id, actor (from SAML NameID), role context, action, resource path, outcome, and reason if failure. You can augment with session IDs and raw SAML assertion if you need.
[00:05:23] Priya: Regarding service accounts, we want them to be identifiable and rotate credentials. Can SCIM handle service-account metadata?
[00:05:30] Omar: Yes, SCIM supports custom schemas so you can annotate service accounts with owner, expiration, and rotation schedule. For longer-lived secrets we strongly recommend customer-managed KMS and enforced key rotation.
[00:05:42] Maya: I also want to surface rollout strategy — for a large org we don't recommend flipping on SCIM for all roles at once. Start with a pilot group and incrementally extend.
[00:05:50] Priya: Agreed. We'll pilot with infra and data teams first.
[00:05:53] Omar: For the pilot we propose: 1) Okta metadata exchange, 2) Redwood sends mapping template, 3) SCIM on for two groups, 4) verify audit exports and SIEM ingestion, 5) cutover for additional groups.
[00:06:06] Amir: On SAML assertions, what about session length and re-auth? We have MFA policies at 12 hours.
[00:06:12] Omar: We honor the session duration from the IdP but also support token lifetimes on Redwood for shorter sessions if you want. MFA enforcement happens at the IdP.
[00:06:20] Maya: Let's capture the follow-ups: Omar will draft mapping YAML, Maya will share pricing, Priya will send Okta metadata — correct?
[00:06:29] Priya: Yes.
[00:06:30] Liam: Also confirm SIEM endpoint format.
[00:06:33] Omar: We'll include Splunk HEC example and a syslog sample.
[00:06:37] Nina: One compliance nuance — we need evidence of key rotation and KMS's tamper logs for audit. Is that available?
[00:06:44] Omar: For customer-managed KMS, rotation logs come from your KMS provider; we can correlate with Redwood logs showing key usage. For HSMs we can provide attestation metadata.
[00:06:54] Priya: Any caveats for Private deployment network setup? We want minimal open ports.
[00:06:59] Omar: Private needs only egress for updates and maybe control-plane connectivity if you choose hybrid. We'll send a hardened network checklist.
[00:07:06] Amir: Regarding role escalation, can we require approvals inside Redwood before a role grant is effective?
[00:07:12] Omar: Yes — we have workflows to require approver sign-off which can be gated via SSO group membership or external ticketing integration.
[00:07:19] Maya: We touched on SOC 2/ISO. Sofia, from CSM, do you want to mention the artifacts we typically attach?
[00:07:24] Sofia: Sure — summary SOC 2 report, ISO scope doc, encryption and key flow diagram, and the RBAC template. We'll attach redacted reports for initial review.
[00:07:34] Nina: We'll need the SOC 2 evidence list mapped to our control IDs.
[00:07:37] Maya: We'll produce a control mapping spreadsheet matching your list.
[00:07:41] Priya: One last item — can we test a simulated breach playbook with full audit trace?
[00:07:47] Omar: We can run a tabletop and produce logs forensics; for pilot we'll include a short sim.
[00:07:52] Amir: That's great.
[00:07:54] Maya: Ok, we'll wrap with next steps and owners — Omar, can you take the lead technical on mapping?
[00:08:00] Omar: Yep, I'll post the mapping YAML and sample SCIM patch examples.
[00:08:03] Maya: Priya, you'll share Okta artifacts by 3/10.
[00:08:06] Priya: Yes.
[00:08:07] Maya: Any other questions?
[00:08:09] Liam: One small note — watch for SCIM attribute name collisions with existing apps, we'll sanitize names.
[00:08:15] Omar: We'll include a sanitization guide.
[00:08:18] Maya: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the artifacts and schedule the pilot kickoff.
[00:08:25] Priya: Thanks.
[00:08:27] Nina: Thanks.
[00:08:28] Amir: Bye.
[00:08:30] [call ends — remainder of time used for Q&A and side discussion between Priya and Amir about Okta groups — truncated by recording]

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcript had noise on acronyms (KMS sometimes transcribed as K M S, HSM as H-S-M, KV cache as K V cash), and a few speaker overlaps. The core technical items above were validated live and will be sent as artifacts.
